summary: After each start, a fleet member starts, restarts, retires and records the end of none of its seats until it has caught up with a peer; it still adopts live runtimes. After five minutes it raises an alert, and a person or an agent can let it go on without unreachable peers for that start with `st fleet admit-without`, a new member.admission-override claim

schema.detail: New claim kind member.admission-override on host subjects (fields start, peers, reason; authorized-requester; append). No table change.

rules.detail: Checkpoint rules and digests are unchanged.

compatibility.detail: An older member keeps member.admission-override retryable until it upgrades, as it does for any unknown kind; nothing older reads it, and only the named member acts on it. New route POST /v1/fleet/admission-override and command `st fleet admit-without`. A member with peers now waits after start until it has caught up with one, which is usually its first exchange.

downtime.detail: A restarted member's seat starts wait for its first complete exchange with a peer; running seats are adopted at once.

manual.detail: No manual step. If every peer of a restarted member is unreachable, its seats wait, an alert names the peers, and an operator applies `st fleet admit-without` on that member.

recovery.detail: An older build acts on its seats' placement at once after a start, as before.
